Surveillance status: partial (IHR notification of cholera in force; the westward-to-eastward spread of the pandemic was being tracked by WHO WER). source: Bono Coulm Coulanges Sirol Tachon (rapp. Felix) 1971 Installation du cholera aux alentours du lac Tchad - Informations preliminaires Bull Soc Pathol Exot 64(4):387-398
processing_notes: Source states: 'En date du 24 juin alors que le foyer Est pouvait être considéré comme bien contrôlé et en très nette régression, son prolongement Nord restait inquiétant. Les chiffres officiellement recueillis sont alors de 6.040 cas dont 2.172 décès pour ce foyer.' - interpreted as 6040 sCh cases, 2172 deaths. Le foyer Nord of the 1971 epidemic: started at Gelirie (village 50 km east of the lake) 'vers le 25 mai' (TL), spread on a ~100 km front along the markets of Tourba, Kameron, Gelirie, Baladja (3-12 June; 4,836 cases/1,586 deaths by 15 June in a ~50,000 km2 zone of ~40,000 inhabitants), then north to N'Gouri (15 June) and west to Delboumou near Cheddra (21 June: 64 cases, 25 deaths in 24 h). Localities fall in today's Hadjer-Lamis (Tourba, Gelirie, Massakory), Lac (N'Gouri) and Barh-El-Gazel (Cheddra), so encoded with the JHU multi-unit convention; 1971 prefectures differ (Chari-Baguirmi, Lac, Kanem). Second independent source: Felix 1971 BSPE 64:571 (Gallica bpt6k9775379d f581): 'causant officiellement en date du 24 juin 6.040 cas et 2.172 décès'. CFR 36% reflects remote villages reached only after mass deaths ('185 décès avant tout secours' at Tourba; no treatment access) - down-weighted to 0.6. Parts check: this focus plus the southern extension (~250/50) and Fort-Lamy (<300/30) = ~6,590/2,252 <= Bono national '> 8.000 cas ; > 2.500 décès' at 24 June and WHO annual 1971 8,230/2,411. source: IRIN Chad-Guinea At wet season's end cholera returns 3 November 2006
processing_notes: Source states: 'Authorities in Chad have tallied 1,201 cases with 60 dead between June and October. The highest number occurred in the southwest in the Hadjer-Lamis region where authorities confirmed 558 cases with 28 dead.' - interpreted as 558 sCh cases, 28 deaths. Provincial cumulative for the 2006 epidemic, June-October 2006, as reported by the Chadian authorities to IRIN (3 Nov 2006). CONFLICT: the MoH DSIS 2006 yearbook (meta 39) gives only Hadjer Lamis 31 cases/11 deaths and Lac 221/15 for 2006 (Agent 1 rows 119-121), while WHO annual 2006 = 1668/71 (JHU) and the national authorities' tally here is 1201/60 to October; the yearbook evidently omits most of the epidemic, so this higher figure is kept at reduced confidence (0.5, single news source) and both numbers are recorded. Agent 1 row 121 (Hadjer-Lamis 7-15 Jun 2006, 31/11) is nested inside this window - do not sum with it. Geographic arithmetic: Hadjer-Lamis 558 + Lac 221 = 779 <= national 1201 (Jun-Oct) <= WHO annual 1668. Provincial subset - do not sum with national row.
